It is therefore connected left terminal -> n1 (left border) and right terminal -> n10 (gate of MOSFET 9). That is the only pairing that leaves no dangling wire end and gives the current source a return path. MOSFET reading: every MOSFET here is drawn as gate plate | oxide gap | three channel segments, with the leads coming off the channel segments on the side AWAY from the plate and the substrate (middle, arrowed) segment tied to the outer segment on the LEFT. So in every case left lead = source, right lead = drain, and terminals are listed (drain, gate, source). MOSFETs 5, 11, 13 (N) have the plate above and the arrow pointing toward it; MOSFETs 6, 7, 9 (P) have the plate on the far side and the arrow pointing away from it - 9's and 7's plates are BELOW the channel, which is why their gate leads exit downwards. Judgment calls: (a) The horizontal at y~248 crosses two verticals, at (210,250) (MOSFET 11's gate lead) and at (306,250) (MOSFET 5's source column). Both carry clearly drawn semicircular hops, so the gate rail n4 does NOT touch n2 or n7 there. (b) The crossing at (312,313), where MOSFET 5's source column crosses the MOSFET-11-drain/MOSFET-6-source diagonal, carries NO hop and NO dot. I read it as a CROSSING (n6 and n7 stay separate). Reasons: neither stroke terminates there - both run straight through - whereas every junction elsewhere in this drawing is a T with one stroke ending on the other; and both readings simulate, so the ink decides. If it were meant as a junction the drafter would have had to draw a dot, and none is present at 16x. (c) MOSFET-P 7 is tiny (35x27 px) and its source and drain wires almost merge into a single 1-2px line at y=444-445. I read it as a series element in that horizontal - source lead going left to the left border, drain lead going right to Resistor 3's bottom and MOSFET 9's source - exactly like the other five MOSFETs, which are all series elements in a horizontal run with the gate perpendicular. The structural fingerprint confirms it: stems at y446-450, channel segments at y451-452, oxide gap at y453-454, gate plate at y455-456 with the gate lead leaving its left end at x=106, which is the exact mirror of MOSFET-P 9 (plate y471-473, gap y467-470, segments y464-466, stems y456-463, gate lead off the plate's left end at x=232). The alternative - treating y=444-445 as one unbroken wire - would short MOSFET 7's drain to its source and leave it carrying no current, which the protocol says is almost certainly the wrong reading. (d) Known Tier-2 findings, kept because the ink is unambiguous: n9 and n10 each consist of a MOSFET gate plus one terminal of an AC current source, so neither has a DC path to ground (a MOSFET gate is an insulator and a current source is an open at DC). simcheck flags both. That is genuinely what is drawn: I-AC 4 drives MOSFET 7's gate and I-AC 10 drives MOSFET 9's gate, each returning to the left-border node n1. Both current sources do have a return path (n1 carries six terminals), so this is the AC-analysis 'no DC path' case, not a mis-trace.
